title: IPv6 NDP: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: I P version six has no A R P. So who finds out which M A C goes with which address? The neighbour discovery protocol does.

scenes.heading: Apartment building directory
scenes.narration: Every resident has an apartment number. A neighbour solicitation asks who owns this apartment. A neighbour advertisement is the answer. A router solicitation asks if any router is around. And a router advertisement announces the prefix and gateway.

scenes.heading: Message types
scenes.narration: These are all I C M P version six messages. Router solicitation is type one thirty three. Router advertisement is one thirty four. Neighbour solicitation is one thirty five. And neighbour advertisement is one thirty six.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. N D P uses multicast, never broadcast. Stale only means reachability isn't confirmed recently. And routers send advertisements on a timer as well.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva IPv6 NDP lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. N D P replaces A R P in I P version six. It uses I C M P version six, and multicast. D A D checks nobody else owns your address. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva IPv6 NDP lab.
